title: Electric-vehicle chain

chokepoint.physics: Assembly is switchable and localises near demand; the real chokepoint is upstream (battery/magnet)

eyebrow: Product-chain pilot · the car that plugs in
h1: An EV is a battery with a car around it
deck: The electric car's supply story is mostly two chains it contains: the battery pack (its costliest part and its real chokepoint) and the magnet motor. On top of those, assembly itself has concentrated — China builds about 70% of the world's electric cars — while most EVs are sold near where they are made.
byline: battery (its own chokepoint) ≠ magnet motor (substitutable) ≠ assembly (~70% CN) ≠ sold near home
correction: Chasing 'EV minerals' misses where the dependence sits. The battery is ~40% of the value and carries the lithium/nickel/cobalt/graphite chokepoint (see the battery chain); the traction motor uses magnet rare earths (see the magnet chain) — but that one is substitutable with induction or wound-rotor designs. The newest concentration is plain assembly: China makes ~70% of the cars.

panels.text: Of roughly 22 million electric cars made in 2025, about 16 million were built in China, which also exported more than 2.5 million — around 40% of world EV exports. So beyond the battery and magnet chains it contains, the EV has a concentration of its own at the point of final assembly, backed by the deepest local supplier base.

panels.h3: The battery is the real dependency
panels.text: The pack is the single most expensive part of an EV and the one with the deepest supply chain — lithium, nickel, cobalt and graphite, refined and assembled ~80–90% in China. Securing 'EV supply' mostly means securing that battery chain; the rest of the car is conventional automotive manufacturing that many countries already do.

sections.h2: 2 · The motor: a chokepoint you can design around

panels.text: Most EVs use permanent-magnet synchronous motors, tying them to neodymium and dysprosium (the magnet chain). But Tesla, Renault and others ship induction or externally-excited wound-rotor motors that use no magnet rare earths at all. The rare-earth exposure in an EV is therefore a design choice — unlike the battery, it can be engineered out.

panels.h3: Cars are made near where they're sold
panels.text: Only about a quarter of electric cars cross between major regions — automakers localise assembly behind tariffs and to be near customers. So EV trade flows look diversified even though the upstream (batteries, cells, magnets) is highly concentrated. The finished-car map is the least informative layer of this chain; the battery and magnet maps are the real ones.
panels.flag: the finished-car map hides the upstream

trade_intro: BACI carries electric passenger cars (HS 870380) and lithium-ion batteries (850760), but a finished EV's origin is its assembly plant, which sits atop battery and magnet chains that customs data does not decompose. Read the shares below as assembly/trade positions, not the upstream concentration that actually constrains the car.
